answer: The ivory multiplier is published, charged in quill, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1900 identities would post 3907 proofs and burn roughly 18 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
